label: paragraph_title
text: POST-STRIKE TRADE.

label: text
text: Opposition at Wuchow Withdrawn.

label: text
text: OBEYING CANTON'S ORDER.

label: text
text: Prediction of Improvement by Next Week.

label: text
text: Instructions by the Strike Committee in Canton have resulted in the withdrawal of "boycott" restrictions at Wuchow.

label: text
text: Gratification is derived from the fact that, in response to a telegram asking for guidance, Anton replied that cargo from a Hong Kong ship could be landed without hindrance.

label: text
text: An expert on Canton, and river shipping predicts with a good deal of confidence that next week will show material improvement in the process of trade resumption with Hong Kong.

label: text
text:
By then, he thinks, opportunities will be forthcoming for Canton traders to put out "feelers" and it is felt that there will be no cause to discourage them.
Latest reports follow:—

label: text
text:
The g.s. "Fook On" was delayed several days at Wuchow before her cargo could be landed.
Cargo coolies and sampan men (members of the transport union) refused to work the "Fook On" at first until an assurance was cabled (in reply to a request) by the Canton Strike Committee that "the boycott was over."
As reported yesterday, surtax was not collected and expectations are that steamers will now be bringing down cargo freely from Wuchow to Hong Kong.

label: text
text:
It is noteworthy that the one boat has left the Canton-Wuchow run to return to the Hong Kong-Wuchow trade.
Livestock, poultry, produce and firewood are shipped extensively down from Wuchow.

label: text
text: From a reliable source the "China Mail" learns that about 20 labourers, suspected to be strike pickets, have been active during the last few days.

label: text
text: The allegation against them is that they are attempting to prevent sampans and junks from intercourse with incoming British steamers, having even gone to the extent of cutting the ropes of the native craft when such were made fast to British steamers.

label: text
text: Both in Hong Kong and Canton, Chinese merchants have been inquiring about shipping cargo by the s.s. "Taishan" next week when she takes up the night run. In the past night-boats have carried nearly all the cargo, simply because they have practically all day in which to load and discharge.

label: text
text: In addition to strictly native cargo, big shipments of produce (such as silk) are carried by the night steamers, for re-export from Hong Kong.

label: text
text: Shameen Servants

label: text
text:
Several hundreds of office and domestic servants are reported to have returned to Shameen since the "settlement of the boycott."
The majority of employers, however, can only maintain a reduced staff at present. Until normal conditions have been fully restored it is thought that many applicants will be refused.

label: text
text: Compradore departments and clerks (where re-engaged) are said to be working smoothly.

label: text
text: In some instances, Chinese servants have been asked to put up deposits to guarantee their good faith.

label: text
text: Traffic is not interfered with but the quantity of cargo moved is still small.

label: text
text: They have been told that it is inadvisable to do so pending the establishment of a Government bureau to collect the surtaxes. Accordingly only paserigers are being carried on to run between Kongmoon and Hong Kong.

label: text
text: More or less obeying the strike branch organisation there, merchants at Kongmoon are not handling cargo just yet.

label: text
text: The s.s. "Tai Let" is announced to sell from Hong Kong, for the first time since the strike, on Sunday.

label: paragraph_title
text: NARROW ESCAPE.

label: paragraph_title
text: CYCLIST THROWN UNDER TRAM CAR.

label: text
text: EMERGES ALIVE.

label: text
text: A young Chinese riding a push bicycle had a miraculous escape from death opposite the Admiral Line offices at Des-Voeux Road about 8:30 this morning.

label: text
text: The cyclist, dressed in European clothes, was coming into town when his mine skidded on the tramway track with the watering of the road in the morning and was thrown in the middle of the track in front of tram car No. 17 proceeding to Causeway Bay.

label: text
text: The "motorman" promptly applied his brakes, but the car had already gone half its length over the youth before it was brought to a halt.

label: text
text:
Passengers on the car and in another which had crossed shortly before the accident gathered round and were surprised to see the youth scramble out alive.
The youth had a cut over the eye and was bleeding through the nose, but beyond this he was none the worse for the mishap and was able to walk to the dispensary to have his wounds dressed.

label: text
text: The machine fell clear of the track and was slightly damaged. Two European schoolboys assisted in straightening the handle bar of the machine and the cyclist wheeled it along.

label: paragraph_title
text: NO PICKETING

label: text
text: Strikers Forbidden to Carry Firearms

label: text
text: As the result of extensive inquiries made in Canton city, a Chinese merchant assures the "China Mail" that there is no picketing whatsoever, nor are any agitators going the rounds of shops to promote a boycott.

label: text
text: There is no intimidation but workers who are members of unions are still afraid to handle British and/or Hong Kong cargoes.

label: text
text:
The Commissioner of Police (Li Cheung-tat) has forbidden pickets to go about with arms.
This order is to prevent the possibility of trouble breaking out—"Wah Tsz Yat Po."

label: paragraph_title
text: TRADE INDICATIONS.

label: text
text: Price Fluctuations of Various Commodities.

label: text
text: Prices of various commodities of trade have changed somewhat this week, partly because of the withdrawal of the blockade "but mainly on account of the severe drop in exchange.

label: text
text: Flour: Stocks are plentiful in Canton, because merchants there have been getting direct shipments from Shanghai and American (Pacific coast) ports. The drop in exchange had resulted in local prices appreciating about 10 cents per bag of 50 lbs.

label: text
text: Vegetables: Additional sources of supply being now available to Hong Kong through the resumption of shipping, prices have shown a fairly substantial drop during the last two days. Shipments are now coming here regularly.

label: text
text: Firewood: Prices are still high. Before the strike, Hong Kong received the majority of the firewood export from Wuchow. Although ships have come down from Wuchow, they brought no firewood.

label: text
text: The Diplomatic Corps has for several days past discussed the Canton surtaxes. It is understood that the matter was again referred to the home Governments yesterday.

label: text
text: It is believed that if unanimity is reached identical notes will be presented through the Consuls at Canton

label: text
text: Chinese official opposition to the surtaxes is growing owing to the belief that the proceeds will be used sooner or later for the war against the North.

label: text
text: Unofficial opinion in foreign circles is also increasingly stronger against the surtaxes fearing that if they are even tacitly admitted they will soon be increased to ten or twenty per cent, thus strangling trade almost as effectually as the boycott did.

label: paragraph_title
text: Last Week's Rumours.

label: text
text:
Reports which have arrived by mail (delayed in transit) throw light on the confused situation in the Kiangsi zone last week.
After making considerable headway along the Yangtse, it will be recalled, Marshal Sun Chuan-fang's army withdrew to hold a front of 100 miles or so between Nanchang'and Kiukiang.
Says the. "Central China Post"

label: paragraph_title
text: PEACE SURMISES.

label: text
text: A long term of quiet along battle fronts in China generally foreshadows untoward happenings, the ultimate result of negotiations which have been going on behind the scenes. Thus it is rather a coincidence that active fighting seemed suddenly to stop just when a determined effort by the Northerners would have relieved Wuchang and that there are persistent rumours to the effect that all is not right in Southern ranks.

label: text
text: - General Tang Sang-chi (8th Nationalist Army) has sent an invitation to Marshal Sun Chuan-fang's chief-of-staff to come up to Hankow to talk peace arrangements. Thus the indications are that there is some rapprochement between Tang and the North against General Chang Kai-shek and the South.

label: text
text:
$ ^{0} $ Weakness Somewhere.
The explanation which is going round Chinese circles is that Chang Kai-shek, through his recent pushes against Kiangsi, has now used up his best units which have suffered very heavy casualties. He now finds that instead of controlling the predominance of power he is not so strong as his lieutenant Tang, who not only has large forces in the field but also has control of the Hanyang Arsenal. Thus Tang is placed in the position of deciding whether the anti-Northern campaign should be carried on further or that negotiations should be started with the Northerners. Naturally, if the Southern position was good it would be worth while carrying on the campaign; but these rumours of peace overturns.

label: paragraph_title
text: GREAT HONOUR."

label: text
text: K.O.S.B.'S COLONEL SPEECH ON ARRIVAL.

label: text
text: WELCOME TO HONG KONG.

label: text
text: His Majesty's transport "Neuralia" presented a gay sight this afternoon when shortly after one o'clock, she was seen towards the eastern entrance to the harbour, her decks lined with khakic-clad soldiers. Her passage through the harbour was necessarily slow, and as she approached, dipping her ensign to H.M. warships, one could hear the strains of the pipe and drum band of the 2nd Batt. the King's Own Scottish orders, the Regiment which is to take over garrison duty from the First Batt. East Surreys, who are sailing for India on the same vessel next week.

label: text
text: The vessel tied up shortly after half past one, but it was not until two o'clock that the Colonel of the Regiment, Lieut.-Col. L. J. C. Comyn, C.M.G., D.S.O., stepped across the gang-way for the purpose of inspecting a Guard-of-Honour of the Scottish Company, H.K.V.D.C., comprising fifty men under Captain D.C. Logan, M.C.

label: text
text: Colonel Comyn passed through the ranks of the detachment, afterwards addressing the men as follows: —Captain Logan and members of the Scottish Company of the Hong Kong Volunteers; My Regiment feel very highly honoured that you have turned out to-day to bid us welcome to your Colony. We realise that you are all busy men and that you have been waiting long for our ship to put into port. This, of course, we very much regret. I feel personally sorry to have kept you so long, but it could not be helped. We regard this as a great Honour, and I trust that it will be but the beginning of much intercourse between my Regiment and the Scottish Company of the Hong Kong Volunteers.

label: paragraph_title
text: Sentiments Appreciated.

label: text
text: Captain Logan briefly replied, saying that his Company had come to welcome the King's Own Scottish Borderers to Hong Kong and they one and all highly appreciated Colonel Comyn's sentiments. He, too, hoped that the two units would see much of each other in the future.

label: text
text: The new Regiment was met by a large gathering of officers of the various units which form the garrison here, one of the first to board the vessel being Bt. Col. F. S. Montague-Bates, C.B. C.M.G., D.S.O., of the East Survey.

label: text
text: One Company of the K.O.S.B. were mustered on deck in full marching order. This Company was marched direct to Wellington Barracks, accompanied by the full band of the East Surreys. The remainder will proceed to their quarters later in the afternoon.

label: text
text: That General Chang Kai-shek had become the virtual dictator of the Canton Government was the allegation made several months ago when he drew up a series of resolutions drastically curbing the power of Communists in the Kuomintang Party.

label: text
text: Actions by the commander-in-chief, prior to his embarking on the Northern Expedition also pointed to his having laid down the law in more than one direction.

label: text
text: "Prominence was also given to General Chang's organisation of a political bureau attached to his staff headquarters and there was no denial of this bureau having the real authority."

label: text
text: This week the Central Kuomin-tang has bestowed further “special rights” on the commander-in-chief’s Political Department. The announcement also says to these special rights, “appropriate restrictions are enacted.”

label: text
text: So far it has not been possible to see any restrictions imposed on Chang Kai-shek by the politicians in Canton.

label: text
text: "However, the "China Mail" also learns that General Chang sent a telegram to the Kuomintang Conference in Canton, stating that he was unable to return from the front on account of the importance of military affairs, but he would strictly obey all resolutions passed by the Conference.

label: text
text:
It is a moot point, therefore, to say "whether Chang Kai-shek is a dictator or not. No attempt has been made to lay down the law to him". His word still goes in Canton but the Kuomintang Conference has unanimously passed a resolution that Mr. Wang Ching-wei, the head of the Political Executive who has been on sick leave for several months is to be welcomed back to office.
Indications at the time of Mr. Wang's sudden withdrawal from the administration pointed to more than ill health being the cause. Little was said in Canton. Elsewhere it was openly said that a difference of opinion between Mr. Wang and General Chang had led to a breach.
